proof:
The lifted hull has precisely the stated fibers, since a combination at base zero uses equal endpoint weights and their midpoint lies in $K$. For a containing cap we may tighten it parallel through the selected point. Suppose $a=b$ and put $r=|M|/a\ge1$ by Brunn–Minkowski. At $(0,g_M)$ a through-cap with nonzero continuous normal gives opposite endpoint threshold shifts. Its contribution from the actual middle subset $M$ is at least $4|M|/9$ by 6769574fc1bd9f8d at full mass in dimension two. The opposite middle area of $M$ is therefore at most $5|M|/9$. Use f0399a8f0bae48c6 §1 with its midpoint container equal to $M$, its linear functional given by the continuous normal, and middle threshold at $g_M$. Its nonincreasing residual bound gives the combined endpoint area divided by $a$ at least $4\sqrt{5r}/3-20r/9$, since $2\sqrt{5r/9}-1>0$. The planar section-width credit pk-w34-payments-planar-section-width-credit bounds the same contribution below by $2r/[9(2r-1)]$.

For $1\le r\le33/20$, the residual estimate plus own contribution is $4\sqrt{5r}/3-16r/9$. It is concave and at $r=1$ exceeds one because $12\sqrt5>25$. At $r=33/20$ it equals $(2/3)\sqrt{33}-44/15>308/345$ because $33\cdot23^2-132^2=33>0$. For $r\ge33/20$, the width estimate plus own contribution is $4r/9+2r/[9(2r-1)]$. Its derivative is $4/9-2/[9(2r-1)^2]>0$, and its value at the split is $11/15+11/69=308/345$. A purely base through-cap contains all of $K$ and an endpoint, giving $k+a\ge2a$. Thus every containing cap pays at least $308a/345$.

At $(0,g_K)$ the same full-mass centroid result gives the separate guarantee $4k/9$. As a function of $s=k/a$, the two normalized guarantees have the same denominator $s+2$, and their numerators are $308/345$ and $4s/9$. The first fraction decreases and the second increases, so their maximum is at least their common value at $s=231/115$, namely $308/1383$. The difference from $2/9$ is $2/4149$. If $k\le2a$, direct division of the first raw guarantee by $k+2a\le4a$ gives $77/345$.

If $a\le b$, contract $B$ about any point of $B$ by factor $\sqrt{a/b}$ to obtain $B'$. Then $(A+B')/2\subseteq K$ and the equal-area raw guarantee applies to the subsystem, hence also at the same point of the original source. The separate $4k/9$ guarantee at $g_K$ is unchanged. Normalizing by $k+a+b$ gives fractions with denominator $s+1+b/a$ and the same two numerators as before. The crossing yields $308/[3(346+115b/a)]$, at least $2/9$ exactly when $b/a\le116/115$.

statement: Let $A,K,B$ be planar convex bodies with $(A+B)/2\subseteq K$ and areas $a,k,b$. The mixed measure is their actual area sum on the three integer fibers at $-1,0,1$. If $a=b$, the ordinary centroid $g_M$ of $M=(A+B)/2$ has raw mixed depth at least $308a/345$ at base zero. The centroid $g_K$ has raw mixed depth at least $4k/9$. Selecting $g_M$ for $k/a\le231/115$ and $g_K$ otherwise guarantees normalized depth at least $308/1383>2/9$. For $k\le2a$, $g_M$ alone has normalized depth at least $77/345$. For arbitrary $a\le b$, taking a homothetic subset $B'\subseteq B$ of area $a$ and using $g_{(A+B')/2}$ or $g_K$ gives normalized depth at least $308/[3(346+115 b/a)]$ in the original middle fiber. This is at least $2/9$ if $b/a\le116/115$.
title: Planar equal endpoint areas give a strict bound in an arbitrary compatible middle fiber
